edges.description: Loss of enzyme activity directly lowers glutamine production from glutamate and ammonia.
Reduced synthesis empties the systemic glutamine pool.
The glutamine synthetase reaction is also the high-affinity ammonia-removal step, so its loss leaves ammonia uncleared.
Systemic depletion is measured as low plasma glutamine.
The cerebrospinal-fluid pool is depleted with the systemic one.
The fetus depends on its own and placental glutamine supply; when that is insufficient, brain development is starved of glutamine. The exact intermediates in human fetal brain have not been measured.

edges.description: Glutamine is the precursor neurons use to rebuild glutamate and GABA pools, so systemic and astrocytic depletion leaves the cycle under-supplied.
Glutamine is the amide-nitrogen donor for NAD+ synthetase, so glutamine lack limits NAD+ synthesis.
Uncleared ammonia is measured as chronic moderate hyperammonemia.
Ammonia excess disturbs astrocyte function, including potassium buffering, on top of the glutamine shortage. Its share of the encephalopathy has not been separated from glutamine lack in patients.
Disordered cortical development is seen as delayed or near-absent gyration.

nodes.description: Astrocytic glutamine synthetase converts glutamate taken up from synapses into glutamine, which neurons use to remake glutamate and GABA. With the enzyme impaired, brain glutamine is very low and the neurotransmitter pools cannot be replenished; glutamate is not raised in plasma or CSF and was slightly low on spectroscopy, so excitotoxic glutamate excess is not the documented mechanism. Cortex-specific Glul knockout mice show low glutamate, glutamine and GABA, astrogliosis and then spontaneous seizures.

Biallelic GLUL variants reduce or abolish glutamine synthetase catalytic activity. Missense variants hit conserved arginines in the active site that bind ATP (Arg324) or are needed for glutamate binding (Arg341); residual activity differs between alleles and tracks survival. Mutant protein is over-expressed in patient cells, a compensatory response that does not restore glutamine.

nodes.description: In the two compound-heterozygous siblings, valproate controlled seizures but precipitated hyperammonemic encephalopathy; carglumic acid, a CPS-I activator, lowered plasma ammonia while valproate was continued, with ammonia falling within hours and tracking carglumic-acid dosing. It bypasses the deficient glutamine-synthetase ammonia-fixing step by opening the urea cycle, so it manages the hyperammonemia arm rather than correcting the enzyme defect. The authors could not determine whether carglumic acid works by relieving valproate's inhibition of residual glutamine synthetase or by driving the urea cycle via CPS-I directly, since valproate metabolites could not be measured.

nodes.description: Without functional glutamine synthetase the body cannot condense glutamate with ammonia. Dietary glutamine does not make up the shortfall, because in healthy people it is consumed by enterocytes on absorption and does not reach the systemic pool. The same reaction is the high-affinity ammonia sink, so one lesion removes both a product and a detoxification step.

nodes.description: Homozygous null embryos die at embryonic day 3.5, so the model shows the developmental requirement for glutamine synthetase but cannot model the postnatal human disease.

Brain malformation is visible before birth in the severe genotypes: enlarged ventricles, delayed or near-absent gyration, immature white matter and periventricular cysts. Glutamine is needed for proliferation of fetal cells and for neural differentiation, and GS is expressed in early fetal life. In mice, Glul knockout is lethal at embryonic day 3.5, and loss restricted to astrocytes is lethal three days after birth, so the human disease is viable only through residual activity or maternal and placental supply.

nodes.description: Ammonia escaping the periportal urea cycle is normally captured by glutamine synthetase in perivenous (centrilobular) hepatocytes, and ammonia reaching the brain is captured by astrocytic glutamine synthetase. Glutamine synthetase has a far lower Km for ammonia than the urea-cycle enzymes, so it is the high-affinity, low-capacity half of ammonia detoxification; its loss produces chronic moderate rather than catastrophic hyperammonemia.
